questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to live in a city that was not too small nor too big. Also I wanted to live in a Spanish city to learn more about the Spanish health care system and improve my Spanish. A big plus was that Gijon is located in between the mountains and the sea, so there are lots of great outdoor options!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall my erasmus exchange in Gijon was amazing! The only reason for it not being a 10 was the little information from the hospital before arriving.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: To find the information about my clinical rotations and clinical tutors, I needed to send a lot of e-mails. Some weeks before arrivel I managed to get in conctact with Monica who works at the Faculty of Medicine in Oviedo. She organized my learning agreement and my clinical rotations. Also I got an e-mail from the Hospital of Cabueñes with information about the departments at the hospital.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My first day at the Hospital I went to the secretaría to meet SIlvia (the responsible person for erasmus students). She helped me to get an ID card, uniform etc. At the University we had a welcome lecture for all international students about how to get a student card, bus card etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was satisfied with the orientation from the Faculty of Medicine, but from the Hospital I did not get so much orientation before arriving. I did not know what time or where to show up the first day, for example. Luckily everything was sorted out my first day at the hospital :)

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a little difficult because I was only staying 3 months (most private landlords rent out rooms for a full semester). I will recommend starting early, both on the facebook groups for erasmus students in Gijon, on idealista and milanuncios. I found mine at the univeristy web page where they offered some shared flats for international students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's very common in Gijon and I will recommend living in a shared flat with other Spanish studnets to improve your Spanish also at home. La Arena is the best area if you want to live close to the beach, the city center and the hospital!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many of the flats in Gijon are pretty old, so make sure your flat has heating as Gijon can get pretty cold between November and March.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy. I did everything through e-mails with the Faculty of Medicine.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: See previous comment.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an office you could go to at the Faculty of Medicine in Oviedo to get help. I got all the help I needed from Monica though e-mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not have classes, only clinical rotations. I could choose where I wanted to do my clnical rotations, and Silvia at the hospital was very helpful to make sure I was placed at the departments that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All the details about your clinical rotations will be sorted out when you arrive at the hospital, so no need to freak out (like I did) :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not have classes, only clinical rotations. At the hospital we had some clinical lectures and workshops with a good academic level!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did clinical rotations at Urgencias, Anestesia and Pediatria (12 weeks in total)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Spain there was more time for one-to-one supervision. Normally I was assigned a young doctor as my supvervisor the whole day and we did most of the examinations together.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I did clinical rotations at Urgencias, Anestesia and Pediatria.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Anestesia was really good!! Not that many other students (so you get a lot of hands on and supervision) and super nice doctors!!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I chose to buy a surf board and a wet suit, which was quite expensive, but totally worth it!!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Buses from the cities in the north of Spain were a bit more expensive than expected. Transportation in Gijon, food and housing was cheaper than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The University offered a lot of activities like hiking trips, surfing, water sport, orchestra, choir etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The erasmus group in Gijon organized tapas nights, city sightseeing, trips to Bilbao and Portugal and much more :)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the hiking group to see some of the beautiful national parks in Asturias, join the social tapas nights and some of the trips!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking!! Picos de Europa is a must, also los acantilados del infierno and Parque de Somiedo. Go travel and see the surrounding small cities in Asturias: Ribadesella, Llanes and Lastres.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have lived in Spain before and I lived with Spanish students, so for me it was quite easy to adjust to the local culture. Be open minded, ask a lot of questions and you will feel more and more Spanish :)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sports acitivity, surfing class, hiking or the tapas nights!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The meals! In Spain they have lunch at 15 and dinner at 22. Make sure to fill your scrub with lots of snacks, because there is no lunch break at the hospital before 15.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people!! They are so open and welcoming, and it's very easy to make new friends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Come prepared to the hospital (bring your books and practice some Spanish vocabulary used at the hospital), bring hiking equipments and enjoy the beautiful Asturias!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be able to attend patients individually in another language and to meet so many other students from other countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be "alone" in a new city. The first week where everything was new: the hospital, the poeple, the city was definitely the most challenging one.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I will recommend everyone to go on erasmus exchange. It has been a memory for life!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
